scenario: AITA for playing music in the middle of the day when my roommate has a weird sleep schedule? | So I live in a 3 bedroom duplex with 2 other girls. She wasn’t too happy with her room because it was the smallest and the location but settled because she had her own bathroom. So the roommate downstairs has a very weird schedule. So obviously with the constant changing work schedule her sleeping schedule has became very weird and erratic and we never know when she’s asleep now. So since I can never guess when she’s asleep I often so downstairs in the kitchen and make food and play music on my speaker while I meal prep. It’s apart of my routine through out the day that i really enjoy since I don’t work till 2pm. But yesterday my roommate downstairs texted our group chat and asked us to please stop playing music in the kitchen at any time of the day. My other roommate said sure but I said that’s not really fair because she often plays music too in the kitchen. Both my roommates are saying I’m being an asshole and that it’s the least I can do because I have the best room in the house because it’s the most separate. I honestly think they are being assholes because why should I have to be so quiet I’m the middle of the day!?

Now, the issue is that the roommate downstairs has a really erratic work schedule. Sometimes she works nights, sometimes mornings, and her days vary from 5 to 13 hours. I like to meal prep in the kitchen and play music on my speaker as part of my routine. It's something I enjoy and helps me through the day. But yesterday, she messaged the group chat asking us to stop playing music in the kitchen at any time of the day. She said it wakes her up almost every time and is disruptive when she's awake. My other roommate agreed with her, but I pushed back, saying it's not fair because she often plays music too. I also mentioned that if she wanted to switch rooms, I'd consider it, but I didn't want to. I told her I was going to keep playing music because it's usually during the day and it's ridiculous to have to stop. Now, both roommates are saying I'm being an asshole, and I think they're the ones being assholes because I shouldn't have to be so quiet in the middle of the day. I'm trying to figure out if I'm right or wrong here. Let me think about the possible angles. On one hand, I have the best room, so maybe I should be more considerate since I'm in a better position. On the other hand, I'm using the shared space (kitchen) during the day, and she's the one with the irregular schedule. It's not like I'm playing music late at night when she's trying to sleep. It's during the day, which is a common time for activities. But she's saying it's disruptive even during the day. Maybe the duplex isn't soundproofed well, so the music travels easily. Also, since her room is the smallest and downstairs, it might be closer to the kitchen, making the noise more intrusive. I also mentioned that she plays music too, but maybe that's not a valid argument because the issue is about the timing and the disruption it causes, not who does it more. Another point is that I have the best room, so perhaps I should make more concessions. It's a common courtesy in shared living situations to be considerate of others, especially when you're in a better position. But I'm also entitled to enjoy my space and routine. It's a balance between respecting each other's needs and maintaining one's own comfort. I'm leaning towards the idea that I should be more considerate, especially since I have the best room. It's not unreasonable to ask to keep noise levels down, even during the day, if it's causing disruption. Maybe I can find a compromise, like using headphones or playing music at a lower volume, or choosing specific times when I know she's awake. But I'm also frustrated because I feel like I'm being penalized for having a better room, and it's not fair that I have to adjust my routine just because she has an irregular schedule. It's a tough spot because both sides have valid points. In the end, I think it's more about mutual respect and finding a middle ground. Maybe I can talk to her about times when she's usually awake and adjust my music playing accordingly. That way, I can still enjoy my routine without disrupting her sleep.
